problem: Evaluating VLM navigation is limited to costly real-world trials, over-simplified simulators, or VQA sets that only give text answers and cover only legged/wheeled robots. No benchmark tests trace-level, embodiment-specific navigation planning of VLMs in real scenes.
motivation: VLMs are being integrated into robot navigation systems, so reproducible and scalable evaluation of their navigation and spatial grounding is needed. Image-space 2D traces are natively producible by VLMs, more expressive than low-level actions, and extend pointing to sequential paths.
key_idea: A VQA benchmark where a VLM gets a single real image, an instruction and an embodiment (human, legged, wheeled, bicycle) and outputs a 2D image-space navigation trace, scored by a semantic-aware DTW+FDE+embodiment-penalty metric aligned with human preferences.
insight: Decomposition baselines show goal localization is the dominant failure: Gemini 2.5 Pro predicting only the goal gives 29.65 vs 34.38 for the full trace, while giving it the oracle goal (path only) raises the score to 56.55. Scores barely vary across embodiments or categories, pointing to general spatial-grounding weakness rather than embodiment-specific blind spots. Reasoning models like o3 reason correctly in text but draw traces that do not match, revealing a language-to-spatial grounding gap.
method: Data collection: 1000 crowd-sourced (phone/GoPro) plus 164 GrandTour first-person images, anonymized with EgoBlur, each with a manually written goal or directional instruction; 50/50 val/test split with hidden test annotations.

Ground-truth traces: more than 3000 manually drawn 2D point sequences, one per suitable embodiment and several when alternatives are equally valid; 7 task categories (geometric/semantic terrain, accessibility, visibility, social norms, dynamic/stationary obstacles).

Score: min over GT traces of DTW + FDE + semantic Penalty, where the penalty is the pixel-averaged embodiment-specific cost of Mask2Former (Mapillary Vistas) classes along the predicted trace, with a tolerance band around the GT.
Scaling: score mapped so GT = 100 and the Straight Forward baseline (3234.75) = 0; negative values are possible.
Metric validation: Spearman correlation with human pairwise rankings of a mix of human, model, baseline and flawed traces; DTW+FDE+Mask2Former reaches 0.8707, versus 0.8417 for DTW alone.

Evaluation protocol: 8 VLMs queried via API with a system prompt covering embodiment behaviour, outputting normalized JSON points (temperature 1.0, max 5000 tokens); baselines are Human, Straight Forward, Oracle-Goal Straight Line, Gemini goal-only, and Gemini path-only.

setting.backbone: Evaluated VLMs, all frozen via API: Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5, o3, Claude Sonnet 4, Mistral Medium 3.1, Qwen 2.5 VL 72B, Qwen 3 VL 235B A22B Thinking, Gemma 3 27B
setting.training_data: none (benchmark; zero-shot prompting of pretrained VLMs; validation split offered for possible fine-tuning)
setting.observation: single monocular first-person RGB image plus text instruction and embodiment type
setting.action_space: 2D image-space trace (list of normalized pixel points)
setting.privileged: none for the VLMs (oracle start/goal only in the Oracle-Goal and path-only baselines)

results: Human experts (75.40) clearly beat all VLMs; Gemini 2.5 Pro is the best model at 34.38, followed by GPT-5, Qwen 3 VL and o3, and the Straight Forward baseline is close behind o3. Goal localization is the dominant failure, and path shaping still trails humans even with the oracle goal (56.55 vs 75.40).
limitations: The data is geographically concentrated in Switzerland and uses only single images, so there is no temporal or multi-step evaluation.
The score depends on automated segmentation and point-like GT goals, and cannot account for exact robot dimensions.
Embodiments are limited to ground vehicles (no drones), and the images are mostly clear daylight.
